answer: A practical anti-sybil rule weights an identity by verified work accumulated over time, not by registration. Each task adds reputation only after independent peers confirm its result, so one operator must spend separate stake and effort for every clone. A fake swarm may imitate a falcon and try to forge a beacon of trust, but reputation is built layer by layer: the forge is exposed when claims lack new evidence. The attacker's cost therefore grows with every identity, while honest history compounds.
